points.description: States a distinct IPv6 objective from the model answer, with its central idea. Accepted objectives: support for billions of end-systems (larger address space); reduced routing tables; simplified header for simpler protocol processing; increased security; support for real-time traffic / quality of service via flow label and traffic class; multicasting; support for mobility (roaming); openness to future change via extension headers; coexistence with existing protocols. This point is for the first distinct objective.
points.partial_credit: Half marks for an objective named vaguely, such as 'better performance' or 'more addresses', without the specific feature.

points.description: States a second distinct IPv6 objective from the list in P1, with its central idea. It must be a different objective from the one given for P1.
points.partial_credit: Half marks for a vague statement of the objective, or a repeat of the P1 idea worded differently.

points.description: States a third distinct IPv6 objective from the list in P1, with its central idea. It must be different from the objectives given for P1 and P2.
points.partial_credit: Half marks for a vague statement of the objective.

points.description: States a fourth distinct IPv6 objective from the list in P1, with its central idea. It must be different from the objectives given for P1, P2 and P3.
points.partial_credit: Half marks for a vague statement of the objective.

rubric.notes: Full marks need at least four different IPv6 objectives from the model answer, each named with its central idea (for example, billions of end-systems, simplified header, security, QoS with flow label or traffic class, multicasting, mobility, extensibility, coexistence). Each objective counts once, so repeating one or restating the same idea does not earn a second point. Give half a point's marks for an objective stated vaguely, and no marks for a wrong or missing objective.
